1.88.38.title: lift-lid depth, dashed lines, build package
changes: Lift lid and backer plate depth dimensions sit on the parts, 3" in from their right edge.
Dashed lines use Rhino's Dashed linetype with print colour and print width By Layer.
Ext wall leg caps line up with the top of the Ext Walls.
The build package starts under the cut list, at the same left edge.
Build package pages have 20% more border.
Mirror-image left and right side assemblies are shown once, marked for both sides.
Removable shelf dimensions in the build package sit on the shelf, 4" from its left edge.
A bottom plate capped by the exterior walls now goes on before them.
The red circle marking XY 0 on CNC layouts is now always 0.5" in diameter, no matter the drawing's dimension scale.

New `Ghost` command: pick objects and they show ghosted (see-through gray with dark edges, your Home PC's Ghosted look) in every viewport. The look ships with the toolkit as "FW Ghosted", so it matches on every computer.
New `Unghost` command: only ghosted objects can be picked; it returns them to normal.
Build packages no longer group their parts, so any part can be moved or deleted on its own.

Build package doors page: the "doors are set back" note is now per inset amount. Doors at the same set-back share one note with an arrow to each door; each different amount gets its own note. One amount still gives the familiar single note.
Classifier: on a frame-and-panel door that sits further forward than the others, the stiles and rails are no longer mistaken for wooden handles.
Cut list: a part that fails to draw is marked INCORRECT instead of stopping the whole cut list.

Edge profiles: the cut list now ends with edge-profile sheets, read from each part's own faces (roundovers, coves, chamfers; through-cuts, miters and sculpted leg contours are excluded). Treated edges are red and lettered, with enlarged sections and shop callouts such as 1/8" roundover and 22.5° chamfer.
Build package: on the step that first adds a part with shaped edges, a note says to shape those edges first.
Cut sheets with few parts are no longer blown up: no page prints closer than 1:10.
Build package: parts from earlier steps print light grey; the parts added in this step stay black.
Cut sheets: a dimension that repeats the same span a lane away is removed.
Cut sheets: two cramped dimension labels pushed into the same gap no longer print on top of each other.
Edge profiles: a free-form edge that came out as two halves now reads as one crowned edge; part types whose pieces sit far apart (a base's crossbars) show one of each piece side by side.
Build package: parts from earlier steps are light grey on the placement (WHERE) pages too, not only on the 3D pages.
Build package: every assembly page carries a numbered step title ("4. Core joins the back panel").
Edge profiles: chamfers modelled between 35 and 55 degrees are named by size ("1/4" chamfer"), as the shop writes them.
Edge profiles: the lift-lid front plate is named and ordered as on the cut sheet.
Edge profiles: edge sheets hold more per page (fewer half-empty pages).
Build package: on the step that adds a part with shaped edges, those edges are drawn red on the 3D view; the lift-lid front plate is named in its note.
Build package: earlier parts are grey on preparation pages that show them too (base under the case, sides brought to the carcass).
Edge profiles: top and bottom edges of upright parts (walls, doors, front plate, base stretchers) are drawn as installed.
Edge profiles: each edge sheet ends with a one-line key (shaped edges are red; sections enlarged, dimensions true size).
Cut sheets: after a duplicate dimension is removed, the rows farther out in that stack slide in to close the empty lane.
Build package: red shaped-edge highlights show through the shaded part in Arctic, so an edge on the far side (a rear bevel) is still visible.
Build package: no L glue-ups (R-NO-L-GLUEUP). Each part is glued along one face direction per step. A check reports any violation in the Build Package diagnostics.
The lift lid front plate is a removable. It goes on with the lift lid in the doors step, named "Lift lid front plate", and never joins the permanent shelf.
Light bars are removables (owner correction). They go in with the record well and drawers, are never glued, and the glue check ignores them.

The Admiral's small fixed plate directly below the lift lid front plate is the one exception. It's glued onto its shelf first: "Fixed plate (below the lift lid front plate) joins the permanent shelf".
The edge-profile note no longer runs into the "doors are set back" note on the doors page.
The second shelf glue-up is titled "Permanent shelf joins the interior walls (second glue-up)".
All 12 test consoles: 0 L glue-ups, 0 INCORRECT.
Build package: the removables step names only the parts the console has (e.g. "Light bar and drawers" on Robin, "Record well" on Kathryn).
12 test consoles: 0 L glue-ups, 0 INCORRECT.
Build package: the side-location steps always show the left side first, then the right. Scott, Jeff, Standard-Crosby and Shelley-Kathryn used to show the right side first.
Glue check: metal parts (Robin and Cortney's brass foot caps) are hardware and are never counted as glued.
Door CNC notes: when two door families on one console share an insert type, the file names are numbered ("louvered mesh doors 1" / "2"), so one program can't overwrite the other. Found on Cortney.
Door sheets: on short openings the opening-width line moves up so its label no longer prints on top of the height label (Cortney door family 2).
Title stock order: the back panel is named as sheet goods with its size ("not in bf"), so the sheet is still ordered. Unit-tested; the harness doesn't run the title command.
